title: Upper bound for a product-preserving derived functor on an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be additive and left exact, and suppose the canonical map $F(\prod_{n\in\mathbf N}M_n)\to\prod_{n\in\mathbf N}F(M_n)$ is an isomorphism for every countable family of module sheaves. Let $N\geq1$ be an integer such that $R^pF(M)=0$ for every quasi-coherent module $M$ and every integer $p\geq N$, with $R^pF$ computed using injective resolutions in all module sheaves. Let $RF:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ be computed on K-injective resolutions; a complex is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex into it is null-homotopic. Then for every integer $b$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with quasi-coherent cohomology and $H^q(E)=0$ for $q>b$, one has $H^m(RF(E))=0$ for $m\geq b+N$. No lower bound on $E$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08F7 (lemma-application-nice-K-injective), part (3), upper-bound clause with lower endpoint minus infinity.

proof.text: For every integer $n$ write $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-lower-truncation-reconstruction], $E$ is the derived limit of $(E_n)_{n\geq0}$, with its canonical maps. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-product-derived-limit] to the small ringed site of $X$ and the given $F$: its product hypothesis is exactly the one assumed here. Then $RF(E)$ is a derived limit of $RF(E_n)$. By [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence], for each integer $i$ there is a short exact sequence $0\to R^1\varprojlim H^{i-1}(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E))\to\varprojlim H^i(RF(E_n))\to0$.

source.place: Tag 08F7, label lemma-application-nice-K-injective, proof of (2) and its application to (3).

proof.text: For every integer $n$, [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] gives $H^{-n}(E)[n]\to E_n\to E_{n-1}\to H^{-n}(E)[n+1]$. The unbounded $RF$ preserves this triangle and commutes with shifts by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]; the required K-injective resolutions exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (also for Ab, viewed as modules over $\mathbf Z$ on the one-object trivial site). For a module $M$ and $p\geq0$, an ordinary injective resolution, placed in nonnegative degrees, is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. It therefore computes both $H^p(RF(M[0]))$ and $R^pF(M)$, by their definitions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The shift formula [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] identifies $H^j(RF(M[n]))$ with $R^{j+n}F(M)$ whenever $j+n\geq0$. For $M=H^{-n}(E)$, which is quasi-coherent, and $n\geq N-i$, the groups at the two ends of $H^i(RF(M[n]))\to H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))\to H^{i+1}(RF(M[n]))$ vanish, since $i+n,i+n+1\geq N$. Exactness from [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] makes the middle map an isomorphism. This proves stabilization for all integers $i,n$ with $n\geq N-i$.

source.place: Tag 08F7, label lemma-application-nice-K-injective, proof of (2) and its application to (3).

proof.text: Fix $i\geq b+N$. At the integer index $n_0=-b-1$, $E_{n_0}=\tau_{\geq b+1}E=0$: its cohomology is zero in every degree by the truncation formula [def-kun-truncations] and the bound on $E$. The zero complex represents zero, and applying the additive $F$ to it gives zero. Thus $H^i(RF(E_{n_0}))=0$. Induct upwards on the integer $n\geq n_0$. For the successor transition $E_{n+1}\to E_n$, one has $n+1\geq-b\geq N-i$, so stabilization from step 2 transports the zero group at $n$ to the group at $n+1$. Hence $H^i(RF(E_n))=0$ for every integer $n\geq-b-1$.

source.place: Tag 08F7, label lemma-application-nice-K-injective, proof of (2) and its application to (3).

proof.text: In degree $i-1$, step 2 makes the transition from natural index $n+1$ to $n$ invertible whenever $n\geq\max(0,N-i)$, because $n+1\geq N-(i-1)$. Therefore [lem-pc-derived-limit-eventually-iso] applies to the abelian-group tower $H^{i-1}(RF(E_n))$, and the left endpoint $R^1\varprojlim H^{i-1}(RF(E_n))$ of the sequence in step 1 is zero.

source.place: Tag 08F7, label lemma-application-nice-K-injective, proof of (2) and its application to (3).

proof.text: The degree-$i$ tower is eventually zero by step 3. A compatible family in its inverse limit has zero $j$th coordinate: choose a natural number $n\geq\max(j,-b-1,0)$ and use compatibility with the transition from the zero term at $n$ to term $j$. Thus $\varprojlim H^i(RF(E_n))=0$. Both endpoints of the short exact sequence in step 1 are zero, so its middle group $H^i(RF(E))$ is zero. This holds for every $i\geq b+N$, as required.
